Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: RSL/Standard Lesotho Bank electronic payment integration enables electronic payment of taxes and customs duties through bank digital channels, supporting government revenue collection digitally. ([Lesotho News Agency](https://www.lena.gov.ls/rsl-slb-launch-e-payment-integration/)).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Revenue Services Lesotho's own 2025 e-Payments and e-Filing guides show CIT, IIT, RIIT, VAT, PAYE and customs duties are all payable digitally via mobile money (EcoCash, M-Pesa) and bank digital channels (Standard Lesotho Bank Unayo, other banks' EFT), corroborating the original single source. Code confirmed at 3 (Yes).

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: The Data Protection Act requires breach notification: if personal information is believed to have been accessed/acquired by an unauthorised person, the data controller must notify the Commission and the data subject as soon as reasonably possible (with limited delay allowed for investigations). ([Lesotho Government Gazette copy via NIC](https://www.nic.ls/lsnic/community/policies/Data_Protection_Act_2011_Lesotho.pdf)).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Data Protection Act, 2011 (Act No. 5 of 2012), s.23 mandates notification of security compromises to the Data Protection Commission and affected data subjects "as soon as reasonably possible", with only a limited delay permitted for police/Commission-directed criminal investigations; DLA Piper's regulatory tracker independently corroborates this as a mandatory regime applicable to payment data. Code confirmed at 3 (Mandatory).

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: CBL’s oversight framework explicitly links retail payment systems to financial access and states that modern retail payment technologies are used to integrate underserved segments and achieve financial inclusion goals, with focus on consumer interests for retail systems. ([CBL Payment System Oversight Framework 2018](https://centralbank.org.ls/wp-content/uploads/Payment_System_Oversight_Framework_2018.pdf)). However, no evidence found of formal pro-poor governance mechanisms like mandated consumer representation on LeSwitch governance bodies or a dedicated inclusion/consumer council with decision rights; evidence is more about inclusion objectives than governance structures.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed as Partial. The Payment Systems Act 2014 establishes a National Payments System Council as a general multi-stakeholder consultative forum (not consumer- or poverty-specific), and the CBL oversight framework links retail payments to financial-inclusion goals but sets out no reserved seats, consumer advisory body, or inclusion mandate with decision rights. The 2025 Payment System Bill (before Parliament in 2026) replaces the governance body with a similarly general advisory Council, again without pro-poor-specific provisions. Code confirmed at 2 (Partial).

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: IMF Selected Issues for Lesotho reports that as of year-end 2020 there were 2.2 million registered mobile money accounts and 882,000 were 30-days active (40% of registered), and that active accounts equate to around two-thirds of the adult population (~1.4 million). Mapping “active digital payment users” to the scale implies 50–69% -> value 3. ([IMF eLibrary (2022 Lesotho Selected Issues)](https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2022/162/article-A002-en.xml)).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with fresher, independent survey evidence. FinScope Lesotho 2021 (FinMark Trust) finds 66% of adults hold a mobile money account, of whom ~72% transact monthly, and separately that ~60% of adults used digital payments in the prior 12 months — corroborating the IMF's 2020 estimate that roughly two-thirds of adults are active users, and placing the figure within the 50-69% band. Note the 90-day-specific definition in this variable is not tested by any single source; if measured strictly at 90 days the true figure could sit slightly lower, but available evidence supports keeping code at 3 (50-69%) rather than downgrading on inference alone.
